questions.question: Which Germanic tribes brought Old English to Britain?
questions.explanation: Old English (Anglo-Saxon) was brought to Britain by the Angles, Saxons, and Jutes, who migrated from what is now Denmark and northern Germany.

questions.question: Which event in 1066 marks the transition from Old English to Middle English?
options: The signing of the Magna Carta
questions.explanation: William the Conqueror's victory at the Battle of Hastings in 1066 brought massive French influence and transformed English into Middle English.

questions.question: Which period of English is dated roughly 1500-1700?
questions.explanation: Early Modern English (c. 1500-1700) is the period of Shakespeare and the King James Bible, following the spread of printing.

questions.question: What was a major linguistic effect of the Norman Conquest?
options: Thousands of French words entered English
English lost all its Germanic vocabulary
questions.explanation: Norman French became the language of the ruling class, and thousands of French loanwords - in law, government, food, and culture - entered English.

questions.question: Approximately when does the Modern English period begin?
questions.explanation: Modern English is usually dated from about 1700 to the present, after the major sound changes and standardization of earlier periods.
